Huge.description: kanagata writes a tuple of 9999 items at most: a maxItems past them is not typed, with a note.

NonEmptyHuge.description: minItems is typed where maxItems is not.

ManyRequired.description: A minItems past them is not typed either.

ClosedHuge.description: A maxItems past the end of a closed tuple makes no longer tuple.

ContradictionHuge.description: maxItems below minItems admits nothing, however large.

IfShortHuge.description: The longer arrays a maxItems in if leaves out are any array past 9999 items: else holds for any array, and then where if admits it.

IfShortAtLimit.description: Those of a maxItems of 9998 are a tuple of 9999 items.

IfShortPastLimit.description: Those of a maxItems of 9999 are not, though the arrays if admits are.

NotShortHuge.description: So are those a maxItems in not leaves.

NotMemberHuge.description: And in a member of it, noted where it is.

IfRefHuge.description: Or in the schema a reference in if reaches.

ContainsMany.description: Nor is a minContains past 9999 where every item matches.

SoleMany.description: Nor where unevaluatedItems leaves only the items contains matches.

ManyPatternKeys.description: A pattern of more than 10000 strings keys the object by any string, with a note.

SharedPattern.description: Where a pattern and propertyNames share more than 10000 keys (11,100: two digits at each end), the pattern's signature stays, with a note.

KeysAtLimit.description: An object type is keyed by the strings of the sets of 300 templates at most.

PatternKeys.description: Past them, the patterns key it by any string, with a note.

NameKeys.description: So are the templates of propertyNames; the properties are among the keys.

ManyNames.description: A pattern of more than 10000 strings is string, with a note and no warning.

SharedNames.description: Patterns all keys must match, as an intersection, are more combinations than 1000: the first of the most is left out, with a note.

Dependent.description: An intersection of unions TypeScript builds into the union of their combinations: past 1000, those of the most are left out, the first first, with a note; the other types stay.

BothEnds.description: A reference has the combinations of its component's type: 1000 strings each, so the first is left out, with a note.

Payment.description: Combinations are counted once the kinds of references leave members out: an object is none of the other kinds unevaluatedProperties lets pass. The union of every member's key is the most and is left out, which the oneOf says anyway.
